hypothesis: The write-regime calendar (20260927-054500, bench 8ec0ce2) found the fleet's hosts serving flush-path ops from discrete baseline states (fast ~0.7-1.1 / slow ~2.2-2.5 / lifted ~5ms) switching unsynchronized on minutes-to-hours scales, leaving every lane to anchor its I/O gates on ad-hoc best-dip baselines. Census question: on a fresh fleet of the STANDARD class (16c/32GB ubuntu:22.04), what is the state SET, dwell-time distribution, transition-rate structure, and cross-host (de)synchronization; is the state machine class-structured (which probe classes lift with it); and what KNOWN-GOOD baseline table (per host, per state, per class) should future lanes label their probe readings against. Infra characterization lane: NO product change, record-only.
approach: 3 fresh same-class VMs (hillclimb-hoststat-a/b/c, 16c/32GB/40GB ubuntu:22.04), probe_regime.py (the write-regime instrument, flock-guarded single instance): all 3 DENSE 0.5s ISOLATED fresh+sync_all+rename streams (advisory v1.0 class 1, continuous) + rich 30s samples (fresh4k/64k/256k+sync_all+rename, fresh4k+fdatasync+rename, fresh4k+rename-no-fsync control, append+fsync, repeat-fsync 4KB class 2, cached-read control, O_DIRECT control) with pre/post host counters (/proc/stat steal, meminfo Dirty/Writeback, vmstat, PSI, cgroup io.stat/io.psi/cpu.stat, raw diskstats). NO burst tests (self-induction settled by the source record; ambient census only). Duration 9000s (2.5h bounded: a per-host-state census, shorter than the write-regime 6h calendar). python3 apt install + launch window labeled NON-AMBIENT. Baseline series = median of NON-STALL (<=15ms) dense ops per 30s window; states = 1-D k-means in log space (centroids >=1.6x apart, >=4% of windows; validated on the write-regime raw data: reproduces its bands + its 0.793 stall-rate pearson exactly).
parity_notes: Infra lane, record only: NO product code changed, no product build measured; frozen parity surfaces untouched by construction. All claims are about host/storage infrastructure.

gates.benchmark_ci: RED 0/0 non-applicable TS harness; standing disposition; never called pass

measurements.method: flock-guarded detached probe_regime.py; dense 0.5s isolated fresh+sync_all+rename (advisory v1.0 class 1) + 30s rich dual-class samples with counters; raw JSONL, no transcription; states from log-space k-means on 30s non-stall-median series
measurements.env: cloud-hypervisor microVMs (same platform class as write-regime), ext4 on virtio root disk, cgroup 0::/ (root)
measurements.nonambient: python3 apt install on all 3 VMs ~11:24-11:27Z + probe launch 11:30:31Z; first 3 min of each series labeled NON-AMBIENT (excluded from state/dwell claims)

phase_census_aligned_windows.note: 3-host aligned 30s windows (301); 0=fast,1=slow; all-3-slow enriched 3.4x over independence => episode ONSETS cluster fleet-wide while steady dwells are per-host (the quantified nuance behind the calendar's 'unsynchronized')

series_totals.note: identical trap COUNTS (21/21/21 at 8.4/h) with 16-21 matched pairs per host pair (<=8s): the trap process is fleet-synchronized and state-independent; NO multi-second traps in this 2.5h window (calendar's 19s twins remain sporadic extremes; max observed here 332.6ms)

conditional_state_coupling.reading: a host is 2.0-2.6x more likely to be in its slow state while another host is slow; p50-series pearson 0.24-0.49 vs stall-rate pearson 0.79-0.82 on the SAME windows cleanly separates the two components

excluded: apt python3 install windows and the first ~3 min after launch (install/launcher write noise; the write-regime record showed the same startup class labeled NON-AMBIENT)
validity.notes: probes flock-guarded single instance (pgrep-verified each check); raw JSONL parsed, no transcription; VM clock offsets bounded by launcher_wall handshake (<2s); no product code involved; instrument validated against the write-regime 6h raw series BEFORE this series ran (band reproduction + 0.793 stall-rate pearson match)

outcome: complete - per-host baseline state machine census delivered on the standard fleet class (3 fresh 16c/32GB ubuntu:22.04 microVMs, 2.51h, 15954 dense isolated fresh+sync_all+rename ops/VM + 266 rich dual-class samples/VM): (1) STATE SET = {fast, slow} on all 3 hosts in this window: fast p50 0.878-0.889ms (band 0.71-1.32, p90 1.3, p95 3.1-3.4), slow p50 2.407-2.467ms (2.7-2.8x the fast floor; p90 3.5-3.7, p95 8.1-8.7); no lifted ~5ms band this window (the calendar's lifted state remains documented; p50 >4x fast floor = beyond-census suspect, which covers it); (2) DWELL: episodes 0.5-37.5min, median 1-3.5min (fast) / 2.5min (slow), max 37.5min fast / 22min slow; transition rates 4.8-6.4/h per direction => a state flip every ~9-12.5min on average; (3) THE STATE MACHINE IS CLASS-STRUCTURED: repeat-fsync is STATE-INVARIANT (p50 0.551-0.566ms in BOTH states, all hosts), append+fsync ~0.59-0.61 and fresh256k+sync ~0.97-1.02 also invariant, nofsync-rename control 0.05 flat; ONLY the fresh-write-and-rename durability classes lift with the state (fresh4k 0.88->2.44, fresh64k 0.82->2.22, fresh4k+fdatasync 0.65->2.0); a single 'host baseline' number is WRONG - the known-good table must be per-state per-class; (4) STALL RATES stay HEALTHY-range in BOTH states (fast 1.02-1.30%, slow 1.23-1.72%): the state machine is a BASELINE property, not a stall property - the v1.0 stall-rate/max gates do not see it; only the baseline-lift rule does; (5) TRAP PROCESS (fleet-synchronized per-request flush traps) continues state-independent: exactly 21 traps>100ms/VM in 2.51h (8.4/h), max 332.6ms, stall-rate pearson 0.79-0.82 all 3 pairs, 16-21 matched instants per pair, no multi-second events this window; (6) CROSS-HOST: state sets per-host, episode onsets CLUSTER fleet-wide (all-3-slow 19.9% observed vs 5.8% independence = 3.4x enrichment; conditional P(slow|other slow) 0.60-0.72 vs P(slow|other fast) 0.27-0.30) while steady dwell phases remain unsynchronized - the calendar's 'unsynchronized' was right about dwells, with a quantified episode-phase coupling it could not see (its 6-op sample p50s were too noisy: same-window stall-rate pearson matched exactly, p50-series did not); (7) KNOWN-GOOD BASELINE TABLE delivered per host class + state + class (measurements.known_good_baseline_table): future lanes label probe readings against these documented bands instead of ad-hoc best-dip anchors (the subscriber-floor stopgap is superseded for this class).
decision: Record-only lane (infra census; no product change, no PR, no merge). Advisory v1.1 ADDENDUM adopted for the fleet gate (v1.0 unchanged in its stall-rate/max/host-relative core): (A) PER-STATE PER-CLASS known-good bands: label every probe's fresh-class p50 with its state (16c/32GB class: fast 0.71-1.32ms, slow 1.57-3.08ms band p50 ~2.4-2.5; >4x fast floor (~3.5ms+) = beyond-census - label and treat as suspect, covers the historical lifted ~5ms state); the 2x-lift gate applies WITHIN the state band, not against the fast floor; (B) repeat-fsync is the STATE-INVARIANT reference: repeat-fsync p50 lifting >2x its own floor (0.55ms) is NOT the state machine - it is a trap/regime event (class-divergence gating); use it to distinguish state coupling (repeat flat, fresh lifted) from regime events (both classes hit); (C) DWELL-AWARE re-probe rule: baseline-lift-only MARGINAL (stall-rate still <=2%) = the host is in its slow state; label the leg slow-state and proceed if the measurement tolerates the 2.7x fresh floor, or wait >=10min for a state flip (flips 4.8-6.4/h; episodes 0.5-37.5min, median ~2.5min - v1.0's 2-5min re-probe usually lands in the same episode, so a persistent lift is expected, not anomalous); (D) the fleet-incident trap gates (stall-rate/max, phase-model re-classification at every leg boundary, no-ceiling labeling, never probe back-to-back) remain EXACTLY as v1.0.
